name: preview_timeline
description:
Preview one timeline through independently selectable views of its structure, composed viewer frames, and bounded transcript.

Views
- timeline: tracks and their state, placed items, gaps, layering references, track-bound effects, and visible timeline markers in the selected range.
- viewer: actual composed timeline pixels for exact frames or a uniform sample (default 9, up to 25 frames). Batch an overview or comparison in one call; use 12-20 samples for a broad visual survey, then request exact frames to inspect small text or refine a change. Uniform sampling only shows sampled moments, not continuous playback. Inspect adjacent frames around entry/exit before judging a cut, fade, or motion. Desktop and the Web agent return a complete contact sheet inline with a saved workspacePath for reuse; exact timeline times and FPS remain in the text result. Read or import that file directly. Hosted external MCP returns individual clean frame links.
- transcript: transcript text associated with non-muted audio/video items in the selected range, mapped through item trim, source offset, and playback rate and labelled by track/item/source asset. Coverage distinguishes complete, partial, and unavailable transcript data.

The views are peers: request one or combine them. Defaults to timeline. Passing viewerFrames or viewerFrameCount also requests viewer, preserving the other views. The result reports the resolved views. timelineId defaults to the active timeline. fromFrame/toFrame use timeline frames and define a half-open range; omit either end to use the timeline start/end. Exact viewerFrames must fall inside that selected range. Use tracks to narrow timeline/transcript. When itemIds is supplied, the timeline view returns only those items, without gaps or markers. When a dense timeline structure has more entries than limit, repeat the same range and filters with the returned nextOffset and the resolved state.id as timelineId.

This tool returns facts, not quality judgments. Use inspect_item for complete placed-item properties, read_script/apply_script for speech editing, and inspect_asset for source-media detail.

External MCP viewer note: this connector has no frontend renderer, so the viewer section uses cloud rendering and returns one temporary image resource link per frame. If your host cannot inspect signed remote images directly, download each full shell-quoted URI into a temporary folder and inspect the pixels there. Successful rendering metadata alone is not visual verification. Local-only media and browser-held blobs need a cloud-readable source before the viewer section can prove them.

fromFrame.description: Optional inclusive timeline start frame. Omit to start at frame 0.

itemIds.description: Optional placed item ids/prefixes (up to 10). When present, the timeline view returns only matching item entries; gaps and markers are omitted.

limit.description: Maximum timeline structure entries returned (default 50, max 100).

offset.description: Zero-based timeline structure entry offset (default 0). For continuation, pass nextOffset, use the returned state.id as timelineId, and keep the same range and filters.

projectId.description: Existing project ID from the editor URL or list_projects. Pass this when continuing work on an existing project and the external MCP session is not already targeted.

timelineId.description: Timeline id/prefix to preview without switching; defaults to the active timeline.

toFrame.description: Optional exclusive timeline end frame. Omit to use the timeline duration.

tracks.description: Optional track aliases/ids (up to 10) for timeline and transcript views.

viewerFrameCount.description: Requests viewer and uniformly samples this many frames (default 9, max 25). Do not combine with viewerFrames.

viewerFrames.description: Requests viewer for these exact timeline frame numbers, or "playhead" when turn-start editor state is available (max 25). Do not combine with viewerFrameCount.

views.description: One or more views: "timeline", "viewer", "transcript". Defaults to ["timeline"]. viewerFrames/viewerFrameCount also include "viewer" without removing other views.
